platform: Your dog loves you too. Here's the proof.
note: 48 divergent ideas for Krish to Approve, Improve or Reject. Every idea ends on the real product design, labelled Example. Dog lines follow heartside's DOG_VOICE: I is the dog, you is the person, signed Love, [dog].

ideas.title: Becoming the Mug
ideas.hook: A dachshund sprints at the camera and launches itself straight at a mug on the table.
beats: Slow motion: ears flying, total commitment.
Splash cut: the dog vanishes into the mug.
The mug turns slowly. The dog is now its painting.
Super: Your dog wants to be in your morning.
ideas.line: I jumped in so you'd never drink your coffee without me.
ideas.why: Absurd physical comedy in the first second, then the reveal answers the question the viewer just asked.
ideas.make: Higgsfield or Runway for the leap and splash; hard cut to the real mug render (no AI on the product).
ideas.risk: The splash must cut to the real render, not morph the mug itself.

ideas.title: The Dog's Christmas Shopping List
ideas.hook: 2:14 am. A golden retriever lit by a laptop screen, paw on the trackpad.
beats: Screen: search bar types 'what to get my person who says they want nothing'.
Tabs pile up: tennis balls, a bigger couch, more tennis balls.
Lands on heartside.io and the mug with its own face.
Super: This year, the dog's buying.
ideas.line: You said you want nothing, so I got you more of me.
ideas.why: Uses canon's own line and the most relatable gift problem. The screen is the real store, so it demonstrates.
ideas.make: AI dog at laptop (Higgsfield still to motion); screen is a real screen recording of heartside.io composited in.
ideas.risk: Screen recording must be the live store, not a mock.

ideas.title: Operation Stocking
ideas.hook: A blueprint of a living room, red string, and a German shepherd briefing the team.
beats: Part 1: the plan. Infiltrate, get the gift under the tree before the humans wake.
Part 2: the crew (a beagle on scent, a frenchie as lookout) creep past the stairs.
Part 3: the gift lands under the tree. Cut to the real framed portrait.
Super: The dog's been planning this.
ideas.line: I have watched over this house all year, so this one was easy.
ideas.why: Heist is a format people follow across parts; each part ends on a cliffhanger that brings them back.
ideas.make: AI dogs in a real-looking home, Higgsfield stills, Runway motion on the winning shots.
ideas.risk: Three parts means three times the production. Test part 1 alone first.

ideas.title: Nature Documentary: The Couch Thief
ideas.hook: Hushed narrator: 'Here, in its natural habitat, the greyhound waits for its moment.'
beats: Person stands up for one second.
The dog flows into the warm spot like water.
Narrator: 'The territory is claimed. Forever.'
Reveal: the blanket with the dog's own painting on it.
ideas.line: Your spot was warm and empty, so I made it mine.
ideas.why: Deadpan wildlife narration is a proven share format, and every dog owner has lost a spot this way.
ideas.make: AI dog footage; narration via ElevenLabs voice (original voice, not an imitation of a real presenter).
ideas.risk: The narrator must not sound like any real, famous presenter.

ideas.title: The Court of the Couch
ideas.hook: A tiny gavel bangs. A pug sits in the dock looking extremely innocent.
beats: Charge: stealing your side of the couch, every single day.
Exhibit A: a photo of the pug in your spot.
Defense rests on one argument: the blanket now has the pug on it anyway.
Verdict: guilty, and very cozy.
ideas.line: I sit in your spot because it smells like you.
ideas.why: Courtroom framing gives a clear setup and punchline. The defense is the product.
ideas.make: AI pug and courtroom set; on-screen type in Fraunces; real blanket render at the verdict.
ideas.risk: Keep it to one beat per shot. Courtroom jokes can drag.

ideas.title: Your Frenchie's Honest Opinion of You
ideas.hook: Slide 1: a French bulldog staring into the lens. 'What your frenchie really thinks of you.'
beats: Slide 2 to 4: three cheeky lines in the over-the-top roast tone.
Slide 5: the soft admission.
Slide 6: the real mug with a frenchie painting, labelled Example.
Series: one carousel per breed group.
ideas.line: You are slow at the door, but you are the only one I wait for.
ideas.why: Breed-specific roasts get tagged to every friend with that breed. The product is the punchline.
ideas.make: Footage-free: approved breed examples and cutouts, type only.
ideas.risk: Roast only the person's habits with the dog, never body, money or job (canon).

ideas.title: The Art Critic
ideas.hook: A doodle in a tiny gallery, standing in front of a framed portrait of itself, very still.
beats: Gallery whisper voiceover: 'Bold. Fearless. Clearly a genius subject.'
It tilts its head, steps back, steps closer.
Walks off satisfied.
The real portrait, labelled Example.
ideas.line: I look expensive on your wall, and I think you should know that.
ideas.why: The doodle's 'impeccable taste' character from the canon. The dog judges its own portrait; no fake human review.
ideas.make: AI doodle in a gallery space; the portrait on the wall is the real render composited in.
ideas.risk: The framed art on screen must be the real render, tracked into the shot.

ideas.title: Hold Still
ideas.hook: A 1700s painter's studio. A Jack Russell on a velvet throne, refusing to hold still.
beats: The painter's brush hovers; the dog spins, sneezes, lies down.
Fast montage of 12 failed sittings.
Final: the dog finally poses for one frame.
Cut to the real portrait. Super: We only needed one photo.
ideas.line: I held still for one second, and I want you to know it was for you.
ideas.why: Turns the ordering mechanism (one photo) into the joke. Ends on the actual benefit.
ideas.make: AI period set and dog; the painter is seen from behind (hands only, no product in their hands).
ideas.risk: Ensure no AI person ever touches the real product.

ideas.title: Five Minutes Apart
ideas.hook: The door closes, a violin swells, and a Cavalier slides down the door in slow motion.
beats: Soap-opera close-ups: staring out the rain-streaked window.
Title card: 4 minutes 58 seconds later.
The door opens; the dog acts like nothing happened.
The mug: so you're never really out of sight.
ideas.line: You left for five minutes, and I have never been so brave.
ideas.why: The Companion Velcro comic character from the canon. Every owner of a clingy dog shares this.
ideas.make: AI Cavalier, practical rain window; licensed violin sting from Epidemic.
ideas.risk: None beyond keeping the melodrama to 12 seconds.

ideas.title: The Dogs' Group Chat
ideas.hook: A phone screen: group chat named 'Gifts for our humans'.
beats: The lab: 'I'm giving mine a stick.'
The shepherd: 'Again?'
The beagle shares a link to their own portrait.
Everyone reacts. Last slide: the three real gifts.
ideas.line: I'm giving you my face on a mug, because a stick felt small.
ideas.why: Chat screenshots read at a glance, cost nothing to make, and carry breed personalities side by side.
ideas.make: Footage-free; chat UI built in code; real product renders last.
ideas.risk: Low. Built in code, zero credits.

ideas.title: The Dog's Search History
ideas.hook: A search bar. Auto-complete fills in: 'how to say I love you without thumbs'.
beats: 'can a dog buy a mug'
'what does my person do all day without me'
'is it weird to put my own face on a gift'
Final result: the real mug.
ideas.line: I can't say it out loud, so I put my face on your mug.
ideas.why: Search-bar jokes are fast to read and endlessly remixable into new posts.
ideas.make: Footage-free, built in code; zero credits.
ideas.risk: Low. Fast to iterate, so good volume filler.

ideas.title: Head of Security
ideas.hook: A chihuahua in full threat-assessment mode as a delivery box lands on the porch.
beats: It circles the box with a low growl and calls for backup (nobody comes).
Box opens itself (the person's hands, out of frame).
Inside: a portrait of the chihuahua.
The chihuahua relaxes completely.
ideas.line: I checked the box for danger, and it was only me being handsome.
ideas.why: Tiny dog, huge seriousness: a contrast the eye reads instantly.
ideas.make: AI chihuahua and porch; the box contents cut to the real portrait render.
ideas.risk: The unboxing must cut to the render, never show AI hands holding it.

ideas.title: Gift Wrap Fail
ideas.hook: A Bernese mountain dog tries to wrap a present and is wrapped in it instead.
beats: Tape everywhere. Paper on its head.
It gives up and lies in the paper.
Cut: the real blanket, the dog's painting on it, folded with a bow.
Super: Some gifts wrap themselves.
ideas.line: I tried to wrap your gift, but I mostly wrapped myself.
ideas.why: Clumsy big dog energy ('Working Goofball'). Seasonal and instantly readable.
ideas.make: AI Bernese; real blanket render.
ideas.risk: Low.

ideas.title: Whose Face Goes on the Mug
ideas.hook: Two dogs, one mug, a standoff across the kitchen floor.
beats: Each dog drags the mug to its side.
A tug-of-war over the coffee table.
Resolution: two mugs, one each.
Super: two gifts, 15% off the set.
ideas.line: I'm sharing you, but I am not sharing the mug.
ideas.why: Sells the bundle through the most common multi-dog household fight.
ideas.make: AI dogs; real mug renders; the bundle terms read from the live store on the day.
ideas.risk: Bundle wording must match the store exactly when it posts.

ideas.title: Bark Translator
ideas.hook: A single bark becomes a waveform, and subtitles read 'Translating...'
beats: Bark 1 translates to 'Where were you.'
Bark 2: 'I was worried for 11 whole minutes.'
Bark 3: the soft one, the love line.
Final card: the mug with the dog's painting.
ideas.line: I bark at the mailman, but you get the soft bark.
ideas.why: A translator format invites remixes and duets on TikTok.
ideas.make: Real dog audio from a licensed sound library, waveform built in code.
ideas.risk: Must not imply a real translation app.

ideas.title: The Dog's Unpopular Opinions
ideas.hook: 'Unpopular opinions, by a beagle.'
beats: 'Your dinner smells better than mine, and that is a crime.'
'The vet is a liar with treats.'
'You are my favorite smell in this house.'
Last slide: the real beagle portrait.
ideas.line: Your dinner smells better than mine, but you smell best of all.
ideas.why: The unpopular-opinions format is native on both platforms and fits the Scent Detective character exactly.
ideas.make: Footage-free; breed example cutouts and type.
ideas.risk: Keep it to the dog's own world (no food it was never given, in customer gifts).

ideas.title: Translate Your Dog
ideas.hook: Slide 1: a Border Collie mid-stare. 'What your collie is trying to tell you.'
beats: Four slides, four lines in that breed's own voice.
The last slide: the gift with that breed's painting.
One carousel per breed, 24 breeds already painted.
ideas.line: I hear your car before anyone else does.
ideas.why: Saves and sends among owners of each breed. We already have all 24 breeds painted and approved.
ideas.make: Footage-free; approved breed examples.
ideas.risk: The archetype words (manager, menace, detective) never appear in the line (canon).

ideas.title: Every Dog Says It Differently
ideas.hook: Same moment, six breeds: the key turns in the door.
beats: The collie is already at the door, organized.
The golden brings a sock, overjoyed.
The shiba glances up, then sighs.
Each with its line on screen, then its painting.
ideas.line: I act like I didn't wait for you, but I did.
ideas.why: Shows the product's whole mechanism: the dog's own personality, made into a gift.
ideas.make: AI dogs in one consistent hallway; the six real paintings at the end.
ideas.risk: Six dogs in one shot style; continuity takes care.

ideas.title: The Seating Plan
ideas.hook: Top-down camera: a couch, and a dog already in the middle.
beats: Home after home from above: every dog has claimed the spot.
Gentle music, rhythmic cuts.
The final couch has the blanket with the dog's painting.
Super: Their spot, now on your couch for good.
ideas.line: The middle of the couch is mine, and the middle is next to you.
ideas.why: Satisfying top-down rhythm and instant recognition of the dog's spot.
ideas.make: AI top-down stills, animated; real blanket render.
ideas.risk: Low.

ideas.title: The Dog Advent Calendar
ideas.hook: Door number 1 opens. Behind it: a dachshund's painting and one line.
beats: One breed a day, 24 days, 24 breeds already painted.
Each day's line in that breed's voice.
Comments vote for tomorrow's breed.
Until 3 Dec, each door also reminds: the printed card from the dog, order by 3 Dec 11:59 pm ET.
ideas.line: Every day I wait for you is a good day, because you come home.
ideas.why: A series with a daily reason to come back, built on assets we already own. It runs right through the Christmas window.
ideas.make: Footage-free motion in code; approved breed examples.
ideas.risk: 24 days of commitment. The card cutoff appears on the card only (Krish's ruling).

ideas.title: Comment Your Dog's Breed
ideas.hook: 'Tell me your dog's breed and I'll tell you what they'd say to you.'
beats: Replies in that breed's voice (Krish posts them).
The best replies become tomorrow's carousel.
The post pins the mug at the end.
ideas.line: You picked me, and I would pick you every single time.
ideas.why: Comments are the cheapest signal of interest, and every reply is new content.
ideas.make: Footage-free; radar drafts the replies, Krish sends them.
ideas.risk: Replies are drafted by the engine and sent by Krish (rule 1).

ideas.title: Morning Coffee, Dog's-Eye View
ideas.hook: A low camera as steam rises and a dog's chin rests on a knee.
beats: The person's hand reaches for the mug (hand only, it's real footage or no hand).
The mug turns slowly: the dog's painting.
Room sound only: the kettle, a tail on the floor.
Super: Your dog, in every morning.
ideas.line: My mornings are better because you're in them.
ideas.why: The quietest hook, the product in its natural daily moment. Works as a still too.
ideas.make: Real footage with Krish's mug sample when it arrives; until then the real mug render in a still life.
ideas.risk: No AI hand on the real mug: still life only until a real sample is filmed.

ideas.title: The Snow Globe
ideas.hook: A tiny dog inside a snow globe on a mantel, looking up.
beats: A finger taps the glass (out of focus).
Snow swirls.
Pull focus past it: the real portrait on the mantel behind.
Super: This year, the dog's buying.
ideas.line: Every Christmas with you is my favorite one.
ideas.why: A beautiful, seasonal single image that stops the scroll and ends on the product in its home.
ideas.make: Higgsfield still of the globe, Runway motion; real portrait render composited on the mantel.
ideas.risk: Composite must keep the portrait unchanged.

ideas.title: The Dog's Letter to Santa
ideas.hook: Typewriter type on cream paper: 'To Santa. I don't need anything this year.'
beats: 'But my person does, and here is what they need.'
A list of tiny things only this dog notices.
Sealed with a paw.
Final: the printed Christmas card from the dog, $12, order by 3 Dec 11:59 pm ET.
ideas.line: I don't need anything this year, but I want you to have the best Christmas.
ideas.why: The cleanest Christmas buy: the $12 card has a real deadline and a low price.
ideas.make: Footage-free; Courier Prime type; the real card image.
ideas.risk: The 3 Dec date is approved for the card only.

ideas.title: Photo In, Painting Out
ideas.hook: Split screen: a phone photo of a dog on the left, blank canvas on the right.
beats: A brush-stroke wipe reveals the real painting.
Repeat with three breeds, faster each time.
End on the framed portrait.
Super: One photo of your dog. That's all.
ideas.line: You took a thousand photos of me, and this is my favorite one.
ideas.why: Demonstration is the strongest proof we have. The viewer imagines their own dog.
ideas.make: Example dogs only (never a customer's photo); the painting revealed is the real approved example.
ideas.risk: The 'before' photo must be an example dog's source, never a customer's.

ideas.title: Which Mood Is Your Dog
ideas.hook: One dog, four paintings: sweet, warm, hilarious, over the top. 'Which one is yours?'
beats: Slide per mood, each with its line.
Last slide: you choose the mood when you make yours.
CTA: comment the mood.
ideas.line: I pretend I'm the boss, but you're my whole world.
ideas.why: Shows the real product choice (the tone slider), and invites a comment.
ideas.make: Footage-free; the store's own 'one dog in four moods' set.
ideas.risk: Only uses paintings already approved on the store.

ideas.title: For the One Who Says They Want Nothing
ideas.hook: 'Every family has one person who says they want nothing.'
beats: 'Here's what they actually want.'
The dog's face, on their mug.
Super: From the dog, so they can't say no.
ideas.line: You said you wanted nothing, so I sent you me.
ideas.why: A problem-solution lead for gift seekers who are already looking.
ideas.make: Footage-free motion; real mug renders.
ideas.risk: Close to F02's line. Pick one if both win.

ideas.title: Tag the Person Your Dog Loves More
ideas.hook: 'Tag the person your dog loves more than you.'
beats: One clear image: a dog's painting on the mug.
Caption invites a tag.
ideas.line: I love everyone here, but you are my favorite.
ideas.why: Tag mechanics spread organic reach through exactly the right recipients.
ideas.make: Footage-free; real mug render.
ideas.risk: Low effort, but low-effort tag bait can feel cheap. Keep it beautiful.

ideas.title: The Mug Travels
ideas.hook: One mug moves across a kitchen counter on its own, frame by frame.
beats: Morning coffee, a desk, a car cupholder, a bedside.
The dog appears beside it in each scene.
Final frame: the mug and the dog together.
Super: Wherever you go, I'm in your hand.
ideas.line: Wherever you go today, I'm going with you.
ideas.why: Stop-motion feels handmade and is loved by both algorithms.
ideas.make: Real mug sample when it arrives; until then held.
ideas.risk: Needs a real mug in hand. Hold until the sample lands.

ideas.title: Your Day, My Day
ideas.hook: Split screen: a busy day for the person, an hour-by-hour wait for the dog.
beats: Left: meetings, traffic. Right: the dog moves with the sunlight.
Both sides speed up toward 6 pm.
They meet at the door. Screen merges.
The portrait: the person it waits for.
ideas.line: Your day is long, but mine is just waiting for you.
ideas.why: Split-screen contrast with a payoff when they meet.
ideas.make: AI dog in a home; the person is seen only from behind or in silhouette.
ideas.risk: Avoid the person's face; no AI person near the product.

ideas.title: The Painting Brushes On
ideas.hook: A blank cream canvas. Brush strokes start appearing, layer by layer.
beats: Ears, then eyes, then the nose.
It speeds up.
The last stroke completes the real painting, and it slides into its frame.
Super: Painted from one photo of your dog.
ideas.line: You always look at me like this, so now I look back.
ideas.why: Process-reveal videos hold attention to the last frame, which is the product.
ideas.make: A mask-wipe reveal of the real painting (we never redraw it).
ideas.risk: Must reveal the real painting, not an AI redraw.

ideas.title: The Christmas Card From the Dog
ideas.hook: A real Christmas card with a dog's painting on the front, lying on a doormat.
beats: Text: This year the card is from the dog.
Price and the order-by line.
Story link sticker to the card page.
ideas.line: Merry Christmas, and thank you for always coming home to me.
ideas.why: The cheapest, fastest yes in the range. Pure buy intent with a real deadline.
ideas.make: Footage-free; the real card image.
ideas.risk: Card order-by only: 3 Dec 11:59 pm ET.

ideas.title: The Wait
ideas.hook: A dog's-eye view of a front door. Light crawls across the floor all afternoon.
beats: The dog dozes, wakes, checks the door.
A car pulls in. The tail starts before the door opens.
Cut to black. One line in Courier.
The portrait.
ideas.line: I don't know where you go all day, but I know you come back.
ideas.why: The quietest, truest dog moment. People send this to the one their dog waits for.
ideas.make: Higgsfield stills, Runway motion on the best; room sound only, licensed music last.
ideas.risk: Pace: must earn the payoff in under 20 seconds.

ideas.title: I Can't Buy You Anything
ideas.hook: Voiceover over a sleeping dog: 'I don't have money, and I don't have thumbs.'
beats: 'But I've watched you every day.'
Small moments: keys, a hand on a head, the couch.
'So this year, someone helped me say it.'
The three gifts.
ideas.line: I can't buy you anything, but I can tell you that you are my whole life.
ideas.why: States the whole idea of a gift from the dog in one breath.
ideas.make: AI dog footage, voiceover by a designed ElevenLabs voice.
ideas.risk: A voice for the dog is a big brand choice; it should be one voice we keep.

ideas.title: The Feet
ideas.hook: Close-up: a dog asleep on someone's feet under a blanket.
beats: Seasons change through the window: rain, sun, leaves, snow.
The dog is always on the feet.
The blanket under it is now the blanket with its painting.
Super: Where they always are.
ideas.line: I sleep on your feet so I know when you get up.
ideas.why: One visual, one feeling, with the blanket in the most natural place it can be.
ideas.make: AI shots of feet and dog; final real blanket render.
ideas.risk: Seasons passing must not suggest the dog ageing (canon).

ideas.title: Heartbeat
ideas.hook: Black screen. The sound of a dog breathing slowly on your lap.
beats: A soft heartbeat joins.
Fade up: a dog asleep on a lap, filmed from above.
One line in Courier.
The blanket with its painting.
ideas.line: When I'm on your lap, I can hear that you're home.
ideas.why: Sound-first hooks stop thumbs on muted-by-default feeds because the captions say 'turn your sound on'.
ideas.make: Licensed sound; AI or stock dog footage; real blanket render.
ideas.risk: Sound must be licensed through Epidemic.

ideas.title: To the One Who Moved Away
ideas.hook: A dog lying beside an empty bed in a kid's old room.
beats: 'Your dog doesn't know what college is.'
'It just knows you left.'
The mug arrives at a dorm (the mug only).
Super: Send them the dog.
ideas.line: Your room still smells like you, so that's where I sleep now.
ideas.why: A sharp recipient (kids at college, a partner who moved away) with a clear reason to buy now.
ideas.make: AI empty room; real mug render.
ideas.risk: Must stay sweet, not sad; no suggestion the dog is unwell.

ideas.title: From the Dog, to Mom
ideas.hook: 'For Mom, from the one who never leaves her side.'
beats: One still per recipient: Mom, Dad, Grandma, a partner, the dog walker.
Each with its own line.
Each ends on a real gift.
ideas.line: You feed me, you walk me, and you let me sleep where I want.
ideas.why: Recipient-led copy meets buyers exactly where Christmas shopping starts: who it's for.
ideas.make: Footage-free; real renders.
ideas.risk: Keep each still beautiful, not a template.

ideas.title: Things Your Dog Does That You Never Noticed
ideas.hook: 'Seven things your dog does for you that you never noticed.'
beats: They wait outside the bathroom door.
They sleep facing the door to watch over you.
They check on you at night.
Last slide: the portrait.
ideas.line: I sleep facing the door so I can keep you safe.
ideas.why: List carousels are the most-saved format on Instagram, and this one ends on the gift.
ideas.make: Footage-free; breed examples.
ideas.risk: Behaviors described as warm observation, not science claims.

ideas.title: The Note in the Box
ideas.hook: A real box opens. On top: the dog's note on the packing slip.
beats: Hands lift the slip (real footage).
The gift underneath.
The free digital card on a phone.
Super: Every gift comes with a note from the dog.
ideas.line: I wanted you to read this before you saw my face.
ideas.why: Shows what actually arrives, which is our strongest real proof.
ideas.make: Real footage only, from Krish's real order. Held until the sample arrives.
ideas.risk: Held until there is a real box to film. Never staged with AI.

ideas.title: Silent Film
ideas.hook: No music at all. Just the room. A dog watches someone make coffee.
beats: The dog follows from room to room.
Typed words appear, one line at a time.
The mug, last.
No voiceover and no music, only the room.
ideas.line: I follow you from room to room because every room is better with you.
ideas.why: Silence is the thumbstop in a feed of trending audio.
ideas.make: AI footage with real room sound; real mug render.
ideas.risk: Some viewers scroll on silence. Worth testing because it's cheap.

ideas.title: The Window Seat
ideas.hook: Rain on a window. A dog watching the street, waiting for one car.
beats: Headlights pass, and none of them are yours.
Then yours. The dog's whole body changes.
The portrait of that face.
Super: Your dog loves you too.
ideas.line: I know the sound of your car better than my own name.
ideas.why: The canon's lead line, earned by a scene.
ideas.make: Higgsfield still; Runway motion; real portrait render.
ideas.risk: Close to The Wait. Pick the stronger if both win.

ideas.title: Paw on Hand
ideas.hook: Extreme close-up: a paw resting on a hand.
beats: Pull back slowly to the dog's face.
The real dog turns, softly, into its painting.
Settle on the real framed portrait.
Super: Your dog, kept.
ideas.line: I put my paw on your hand so you know I'm here.
ideas.why: The morph is the most stopping visual we have; the tender version suits a portrait.
ideas.make: Runway morph from an AI dog into the real example painting; ends on the real render.
ideas.risk: Krish allowed one morph. F01 and this one compete for it, unless he lifts the limit.

ideas.title: From Down Here
ideas.hook: Camera at dog height, looking up at the person (faceless), all day.
beats: Feet, hands, a dropped sock, a hand coming down for a scratch.
The dog's eyes never leave them.
The final shot: the dog's painting, looking back up at you.
Super: You're their whole world.
ideas.line: I've seen most of the world from down here, and you're the best part.
ideas.why: A point of view nobody shows, which instantly reframes the dog's love.
ideas.make: AI low-angle footage; the person never shown with the product.
ideas.risk: Low.

ideas.title: Two People, One Dog in the Middle
ideas.hook: From above: a bed, two pairs of feet, and a dog squarely in the middle.
beats: Night after night, the dog in the middle.
The blanket with its painting on the bed.
Super: For the two of you, from the one in the middle.
ideas.line: I sleep in the middle so I can be close to both of you.
ideas.why: Couples gift: one partner buys for the other, from the dog.
ideas.make: AI top-down still; real blanket render.
ideas.risk: Feet only; no AI people near the product.

ideas.title: First Snow
ideas.hook: A dog sees snow for the first time and freezes, then leaps.
beats: Pure joy in slow motion.
Snow on its nose.
Inside: the portrait on the wall above the tree.
Super: The face you'll want to keep.
ideas.line: Everything is new when I'm with you, even the cold stuff.
ideas.why: Seasonal joy that matches the Christmas window and is pure delight.
ideas.make: AI snow footage; real portrait composited.
ideas.risk: Low.

ideas.title: The Grandparent Gift
ideas.hook: 'Grandma has a photo of every grandkid. Except one.'
beats: A mantel of family photos.
A gap.
The dog's framed portrait fills it.
Super: The grandkid with four legs.
ideas.line: You always save me a treat, so I saved you a spot on your wall.
ideas.why: A concrete family gift moment and a recipient with buying power.
ideas.make: AI mantel scene; real portrait render composited.
ideas.risk: Family photos in the scene must be obviously generic, never real people.

ideas.title: What I'd Say If I Could
ideas.hook: A dog looks straight into the lens. Subtitles start: 'If I could say one thing to you.'
beats: A short, sincere speech in its breed's voice.
Each episode a different breed.
Ends on its gift.
Series, one a day.
ideas.line: If I could say one thing, it would be that I'm glad it's you.
ideas.why: Direct-to-camera talking pets are among the most shared pet formats, and this one is sincere, not silly.
ideas.make: AI dog close-up; subtitles only or a designed voice.
ideas.risk: If voiced, one consistent voice per breed.
